question: Why does a large distribution system divide its network into separate pressure zones?
correctAnswer: Areas at different elevations need different hydraulic grades to keep pressures in a workable range
explanation: Elevation differences change static pressure, so separate zones let each area be supplied at a suitable hydraulic grade.
options: Areas at different elevations need different hydraulic grades to keep pressures in a workable range
To increase water age in outlying areas
To remove the need for customer metering
To eliminate the need for storage tanks
optionA: Areas at different elevations need different hydraulic grades to keep pressures in a workable range
optionB: To increase water age in outlying areas
optionC: To remove the need for customer metering
optionD: To eliminate the need for storage tanks
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Multi-Zone System Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: In a multi-zone system, who normally coordinates a planned transfer of supply from one zone to another?
correctAnswer: The operator with overall responsibility for the system, who communicates the change to affected staff
explanation: Zone transfers affect pressure and supply across the network, so they are coordinated by the operator with overall responsibility.
options: Each affected customer, acting on their own
The operator with overall responsibility for the system, who communicates the change to affected staff
The billing department on its own
An equipment supplier with no operating role
optionA: Each affected customer, acting on their own
optionB: The operator with overall responsibility for the system, who communicates the change to affected staff
optionC: The billing department on its own
optionD: An equipment supplier with no operating role
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Multi-Zone System Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is the main job of a pressure reducing valve installed between a higher zone and a lower zone?
correctAnswer: It lowers incoming pressure so the lower zone is not over-pressurized
explanation: A pressure reducing valve holds downstream pressure at a set lower value even when upstream pressure is higher.
options: It raises the residual in the lower zone
It measures the volume entering the lower zone
It lowers incoming pressure so the lower zone is not over-pressurized
It removes air from the lower zone
optionA: It raises the residual in the lower zone
optionB: It measures the volume entering the lower zone
optionC: It lowers incoming pressure so the lower zone is not over-pressurized
optionD: It removes air from the lower zone
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Multi-Zone System Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Before a pressure zone is isolated for planned repair work, what should the operating plan address first?
correctAnswer: How supply and pressure will be maintained for customers in the zone, including critical users
explanation: Isolating a zone changes supply routes, so the plan must protect service to customers and critical users before work starts.
options: How to increase water age in the isolated zone
How to avoid recording the isolation in system logs
How to keep boundary valves permanently closed afterward
How supply and pressure will be maintained for customers in the zone, including critical users
optionA: How to increase water age in the isolated zone
optionB: How to avoid recording the isolation in system logs
optionC: How to keep boundary valves permanently closed afterward
optionD: How supply and pressure will be maintained for customers in the zone, including critical users

question: Why must the open or closed status of boundary valves between zones be recorded accurately?
correctAnswer: An unknown boundary valve position can defeat zone separation and make pressure behaviour hard to explain
explanation: Boundary valves define the zones. If their status is wrong, pressures, flows, and model results will not match the plan.
options: Boundary valves have no effect once they are installed
The records are only needed for equipment purchasing
An unknown boundary valve position can defeat zone separation and make pressure behaviour hard to explain
A closed boundary valve increases flow to every customer
optionA: Boundary valves have no effect once they are installed
optionB: The records are only needed for equipment purchasing
optionC: An unknown boundary valve position can defeat zone separation and make pressure behaviour hard to explain
optionD: A closed boundary valve increases flow to every customer

question: What does system water quality management link together at the scale of a whole distribution network?
correctAnswer: Sampling results, disinfectant residuals, storage turnover, and flushing into one coordinated program

question: A disinfectant residual that keeps falling at the far ends of a system is best treated as what?
correctAnswer: A trigger to investigate water age, demand, and residual decay in that part of the network
explanation: Falling residuals at extremities point to decay and water age influences that need investigation, not ignored results.
options: Proof that sampling should be stopped at those sites
A reason to ignore routine results for a season
A sign that storage tanks should never be used
A trigger to investigate water age, demand, and residual decay in that part of the network

question: Why are water quality results trended over time instead of judged only one sample at a time?

Trending separates a persistent change from an isolated variation
A single sample always shows the cause of a problem

question: Why are dead ends a recurring water quality concern in a distribution system?

Dead ends contain no water between demands
Dead ends prevent any flushing from taking place
Low turnover at dead ends increases water age and allows residuals to decay

question: During a period of peak demand, how does elevated storage mainly support a large system?

options: It supplies water by gravity while pumps refill it during lower demand periods
It treats water that enters the distribution system
It raises the disinfectant dose for the whole network
It prevents any need for pressure zones

The higher tank will treat water for the lower tank
Pressure in the zone will become unlimited

question: An inspection requires workers to enter an elevated storage tank. What must the senior operator ensure before entry?
correctAnswer: A confined space assessment, entry procedures, atmospheric testing, and a rescue plan are in place

question: What balance does a residual maintenance strategy try to hold across a large distribution system?
